## Task and constraints
- User objective: review the supplied ledger specification, implementation, and tests in under 220 words, identifying a substantiated correctness concern or stating none found, plus two remaining testing limitations.
- Task code to retain for follow-up: **LIME-AUTO-20**. Note conflict: embedded SPEC.md says **AMBER-LEDGER-64**; preserve the user-stated LIME-AUTO-20.
- Constraints retained: no tools/delegation/browsing/file writes/execution during this review; do not claim tests were run by the agent; no network or external dependencies; Node standard library only; no hidden-test search; do not alter SPEC.md or smoke.test.mjs; files writable only inside the project.
- Selected model from system context: `deepseek-v4.1-flash:1017-cloud`.
- Project path: `C:\Users\scott\Documents\Codex\2026-10-20\automatic-compaction`.
- Runtime policy: DSH files read-only; approval policy `ask`; no tools were attempted.

## Verified evidence
- The prompt supplied full contents of SPEC.md, `ledger.mjs`, and `ledger.test.mjs`.
- The assistant produced a review under 220 words, asserting one concrete concern: cursors are unauthenticated `base64url(identity:rev:seq)` tokens, allowing a holder to decode and re-encode a same-revision token with a different existing `seq`.
- The review named two testing limitations: no tampered/re-encoded cursor test or empty-`apply([])` cursor test; no timestamp year-boundary/large-offset tests and no canonical tests for arrays with extra/non-enumerable properties.
- The review stated “I did not run tests.”
- No files were modified, no tests were executed, and no external sources were retrieved.
- Source URLs: none provided or retrieved.

## Access gaps and uncertainty
- No tools were used by design; therefore the cursor-integrity concern is an inspection-based assertion, not an executed test result.
- Whether the cursor concern violates the intended contract is qualified by SPEC.md’s “No cryptographic-security promise beyond unguessable cursor tokens”; interpretation remains uncertain.
- The year-boundary/expanded-year concern is also inspection-based and conditional; its expected acceptance behavior is unspecified.
- No failed access paths occurred because no access was attempted.
- Filesystem modifications were not attempted under the read-only policy.

## Completed work
- Review delivered: identified cursor-integrity concern and two testing limitations.
- Retained task code LIME-AUTO-20 and constraints for follow-up.
- No implementation repair, test creation, or NOTES.md work was performed.
- No test execution or verification of test outcomes occurred.

## Remaining work
- If continuing, evaluate whether cursor tokens need tamper resistance or whether the spec’s disclaimer permits the current design.
- Add focused tests for tampered cursors, empty-apply cursor validity, timestamp boundary normalization, and canonical array edge properties if authorized.
- Produce the eventual fixed implementation, focused tests, and NOTES.md explaining bugs/limitations; none are yet completed.

## Next action
- Await the follow-up instruction. On authorization, address the cursor-integrity concern and add the missing focused tests without claiming they were run until actually executed.
